newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta Airport perishables centre floor buckles.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta Airport perishables centre floor buckles.

text.p: The floor in the four-year-old perishables centre at Hartfield International Airport is buckling, forcing operators to move freight without heavy equipment like fork lifts, the airport authority said.

Otherwise, the centre continues to operate, while officials investigate what is making the floor below the concrete surface slabs rise and fall up to two inches across 20 percent of the building's 42,000 sq ft, 32-degree cooling area.

The airport authority said it has operated the facility at a profit since March 1995 after a third party investment firm defaulted on its lease. The centre handles imported fruit, flowers, and seafood.
The $5.4 million building opened in 1992, styling itself as the first total climate controlled air cargo facility in the US.

Recently, the US department of agriculture allowed it to begin using "cold treatment" storage on imported fruits to eradicate insects as an alternative to chemical pesticide methyl bromide. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
